messages:
Maya Chen: Quick kickoff — proposing a lightweight canary lane approach for model catalog cutovers. Goal: let customers opt into a pinned gracepath that lasts 30 days, with an automated fallback to the prior pinned variant if regressions appear. Keep ops overhead minimal.
Ava Ruiz: Love the idea. Can we define the acceptance gates? what metrics should trigger fallback?
Jon Patel: Minimal set: 1) 95th pct latency delta <= 20ms, 2) token-cost change <= 10%, 3) top-1 response-accuracy on our smoke evals >= baseline - 2%. If any gate fails, auto-roll back.
Keegan O'Neill: How do we measure "response-accuracy" in an automated way for arbitrary customers? We need a small prompt set + fuzzy match thresholds.
Maya Chen: Proposal: for the lightweight lane we require customers to provide 10 canonical prompts OR we run our standard smoke-suite (10 prompts) if they opt out. Use tokenized BLEU-ish similarity + hand-picked anchors.
Samir Gupta: Cost angle — pinned gracepath with long TTL means more capacity reservations. For a 30-day TTL we should only allow pinned weight <= 20% of a tenant's traffic or enforce probe-sampling. Otherwise infra costs blow up.
Ava Ruiz: Agree on probe-sampling. Suggest sample 5% of traffic to the new model for the first 48h, then ramp to 20% if gates pass. Documented ramp schedule: 5% -> 20% -> 50% (opt-in only).
Jon Patel: Ops detail: need a canary SLA window and automatic rollback rule in the router. Also add a disable-pin flag for customers with strict budgets.
Keegan O'Neill: Telemetry: we need these events -- catalog.pin.create, catalog.pin.ramp, catalog.pin.rollback, catalog.pin.expire, catalog.pin.metrics.report. Make sure these are in telemetry schema v3.
Maya Chen: Good call. Also requirement: provide customers with a one-click extend of gracepath (+15d) from Console with a warning about cost.
Samir Gupta: For the compatibility shim: small adapter layer to remap tokenizers and fallback to previous normalization. Keep it as a runtime library so Private deployments can drop it if they want.
Ava Ruiz: Can we add a simple smoke CLI for VE teams to reproduce bench locally? Something like: 
```bash
# smoke bench
rb-bench --model <model> --seq 512 --rps 20 --slo 150
```
Jon Patel: Add to that: a `--golden-set` flag to point to the 10 prompts and a `--fuzzy-threshold 0.82` default.
Keegan O'Neill: Ops hooks: tag canary runs in traces, and surface a compact dashboard: latency, cost delta, quality delta, and traffic %. If quality delta goes negative beyond threshold -> auto rollback.
Maya Chen: Timeline suggestion: prototype shim + CLI in 2 sprints, telemetry + router automation in 1 sprint, Console extension + docs in 1 sprint. Total ~4 sprints (cross-functional).
Samir Gupta: Risk register note: customers with pinned heavy traffic may cause scheduling squeezes. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant concurrency cap for pinned variants and allow spillover to older variants if overloaded.
Ava Ruiz: Comms: create a short customer playbook describing the 30-day gracepath, sample rates, extend flow, and SLA implications. Keep language simple for PMs and CSMs.
Jon Patel: Acceptance checklist for launch (Quick list):
- [ ] CLI + shim PoC
- [ ] Telemetry events in schema v3 + dashboard widgets
- [ ] Router automation for ramp + auto-rollback
- [ ] Console one-click extend + cost warning
- [ ] Run internal canary on 2 non-prod tenants
- [ ] Docs + playbook for CSMs
Keegan O'Neill: Who owns the runbook? I can pair with Product on the first draft.
Maya Chen: Action items:
- Keegan -> first cut runbook + telemetry defs (due EOD Wed)
- Jon -> router automation RFC + rollback rules (due Fri)
- Samir -> cost and capacity caps proposal (due Thu)
- Ava -> customer playbook draft and checklist (due next Tue)
- Maya -> coordinate cross-functional demo and internal canary (schedule next week)
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job created for internal-canary-2029 starting at 2029-06-12T02:00Z
Maya Chen: OK folks — thanks. We'll sync Wed 10a to review Keegan's runbook and adjust scope if needed. :thumbsup:
